newsitem.title: INDIA: India launches manhunt after Briton's murder.
newsitem.headline: India launches manhunt after Briton's murder.

text.p: Indian police said on Saturday they were hunting for the Indian companion of a British woman found murdered in a hotel room in Delhi earlier this week.
Police were looking for Vijay Giri, said to be aged between 17 and 20, after 43-year-old Flury Regina Malle was found strangled on Wednesday in New Delhi's congested old quarter.
"Robbery appears to be the motive. There was no evidence of rape. She was living with him in the same room," senior police official Ajay Kashyap told Reuters by telephone.
He said the two had checked into the hotel on May 22 after arriving from Hardwar, a holy Hindu town on the banks of the Ganges, some 240 km (150 miles) from Delhi.
Giri's name, which may not be his real identity, were from the hotel's records, police said.
Lcal newspapers said the killer may have been a psychopath, based on scribbling on the room's wall in Hindi that said: "I have committed 24 murders-Sinner."
Kashyap said other details on the murdered woman were not available because she had reported to police that her passport was lost.
